subject: FW: Urgent — EmberPay SLA risk: dedicated GPU pool backpressure & reserved quota shortfall
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@emberpay.com>

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production errors + latency spike (EMB account)

Soojin,

We're seeing a sustained uptick in inference latencies for our busiest endpoint (generate_chat) starting 08:45 PT — p90 moved from ~120ms to ~1.8s and we're seeing 502 spikes when bursts overlap. Attached is a screenshot from our monitoring dashboard and a short logfile showing queue lengths. We're on a reserved plan and expected throughput has been met historically; this is new and impacting checkouts.

Can Redwood confirm whether the dedicated GPU pool for EmberPay is experiencing contention or if there's an upstream routing/fallback to lower capacity nodes? We need an ETA on mitigation — this is actively blocking 3 merchants.

Alex Turner
Head of Platform Reliability, EmberPay

On Sun, Mar 21, 2027 at 09:28 AM soojin_lee@redwood.com wrote:
> Jonas / David — forwarding EmberPay alert.

Quick triage:
- No scheduled maintenance or autoscale policy changes in the last 24h.
- Observed sustained queue depth increase starting 08:42 PT on pool reserved-ember-usw2-2 (their dedicated slice).
- GPU utilization is at 98% on two nodes; we see continuous long-tail KV-cache churn that is increasing per-request GPU setup time (model warmup overhead).
- There is a shortfall vs. their reserved throughput target: effective serving QPS dropped ~18% when background batch coalescing triggered. That explains the p90 jump and the 502 spikes when backpressure reached our service-side queue limits.

Immediate action taken:
1) Pinned EmberPay traffic to two hot nodes with cache pinning to reduce KV churn (temporary, 15m window).
2) Enabled short-term burst capacity on our spare pool (30% of spare headroom) — will last ~45 minutes unless authorized to extend.
3) Kicked an async job to rebuild the model warmup cache on the affected nodes.

Next steps (need decisions):
- Approve extending burst for up to 4 hours (requires exec/billing signoff for credit/authorization).
- Provision permanent additional reserved headroom for EMB (recommended +20% commit) to prevent recurrence.

I will attach logs shortly.
Jonas

From: david_kim@redwood.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production errors + latency spike (EMB account)

Updating thread with telemetry and impact:
- Confirmed 502s correlate with queue overflow at the request router (service-side). We hit configured soft-queue limit at 08:49 PT causing drops while queue drains.
- Trace shows a sequence-length distribution spike due to a campaign traffic pattern (longer prompts). Avg tokens per request jumped 4x — UVs where we expected 150 tokens spiked to 600+.
- KV-cache invalidations happened more frequently because of the token-length bursts and concurrent tenants warming large context windows.

Temporary mitigation status (09:55 PT):
- Pinned nodes and warmup job reduced p90 to ~350ms, errors dropped substantially.
- Spare-burst is live; we've consumed ~12% of the authorized spare headroom.

Ask for sales/procurement:
Soojin / Marissa — EmberPay will need either immediate burst authorization (to keep checkout healthy through their marketing spike) or a short-term credit to allow us to keep spare capacity applied for 4 hours. If not, we should auto-fail to a lower-capacity variant to avoid 502s, but that will increase latency and may break EmberPay SLAs.

-David

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@emberpay.com>, Contracts <procurement@emberpay.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production errors + latency spike (EMB account)

Alex — quick update and proposed path: we identified dedicated-pool contention caused by an unexpected sequence-length surge from a campaign. Engineers have pinned cache and opened a short burst to spare headroom; p90 dropped from ~1.8s to ~350ms and 502s have mostly cleared.

Two options for EmberPay (short-term):
1) Approve a 4-hour burst window from Redwood spare headroom (we'll apply and bill as overage credits); this keeps you on current model and preserves latency/SLA.
2) Allow our platform to failover your requests to a compatible lower-capacity model variant after 30 minutes (will reduce errors but increase median latency by ~200–400ms).

We’ve drafted a one-page mutual action plan to capture this and a longer-term recommendation to increase reserved headroom by +20% into your next commit (attached). Can procurement confirm which path you want? If you want option 1, we need a reply with \"Authorize 4h burst\" to proceed.

--
Soojin Lee
Enterprise AE (Escalations)
Redwood Inference

Impact: potential SLA violations for a priority enterprise customer. Technical remediation available, but financial signoff needed to keep spare capacity applied.

Request: please approve up to 4 hours of burst credit (estimate $2.5k in overage exposure) so we can stabilize their checkout traffic. If not approved within 60 minutes, we will need to trigger an automatic failover to a lower-capacity variant (customer impact).

Marissa Cole
